assumptions: DORA register obligations and underlying ICT-contract changes create some recurring maintenance work beyond the first reporting cycle, although the frequency and budget are unknown.
A customer-controlled deployment can technically keep sensitive contract content inside the regulated entity's or partner's environment, but this does not imply procurement or security approval.
The founder can obtain bounded regulatory review from a qualified advisor while retaining responsibility for software correctness, release maintenance, and operational support.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid, arm's-length pilot in which an advisor is the contracting payer, brings at least one consenting regulated client, passes that client's security and procurement review, and demonstrates against the free official stack and a priced specialist alternative: lower expert hours and rework, accurate source lineage and exports, acceptable deployment and support cost, positive partner payback, software-like contribution margin, and written intent to renew and activate additional client entities.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Mandatory DORA registers create a real accuracy and provenance problem, and positioning a customer-controlled runtime behind an advisor who retains remediation revenue is a coherent attempt to align incentives and reduce direct selling. The insight is not yet distinctive enough to establish a durable opportunity because official tooling and existing products already address validation and export, while the proposed partner behavior is unverified.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Dry-run failures, Polish resubmissions, and continuing regulator training support genuine operational friction around a compulsory task. However, many failures were limited in count, free regulator materials directly support remediation, recurrence after early reporting cycles is unknown, and there is no evidence that the proposed advisor payer values the runtime enough to buy it.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Partner and per-entity licensing could generate recurring revenue while leaving labor-intensive interpretation and remediation with the prime contractor, and the stated startup capital is compatible with a bounded pilot. Yet pricing, activation, renewal, support load, deployment isolation, gross margin, acquisition cost, payback, and the scale assumptions behind the founder wealth path are all unmeasured; public specialist pricing and ongoing taxonomy maintenance constrain upside.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Boutique Polish DORA advisors and managed-service providers form a clear, narrow initial buyer segment with a defined reporting trigger. The packet does not establish how many suitable partners exist, how many relevant client entities each controls, how much unresolved work remains, or whether the Polish wedge alone is economically meaningful before costly multi-country expansion.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: White-label operation, clause-to-field lineage, and customer-controlled deployment offer a plausible niche position for advisor-led engagements. There is no validated exclusive channel, customer trust advantage, superior workflow performance, or switching mechanism, while free official materials, an established enterprise platform, and a priced DORA specialist give buyers credible alternatives.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful rules-and-lineage engine could extend across additional EU jurisdictions, partner portfolios, reporting cycles, and adjacent third-party contract-risk workflows. Expansion is plausible but not automatic because national submission differences, security reviews, regulatory interpretation, and rule maintenance recur in each geography and use case.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Versioned rule adapters, remediation patterns, clause mappings, and embedded partner workflows could improve with accumulated use. The proposed reusable asset excludes confidential source data, partner contribution is uncertain, official specifications are public, exports reduce lock-in, and competitors or advisors could reproduce the core rules and workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Provenance, deterministic checks, human approvals, and local KNF export in a customer-controlled runtime could reduce rework and security exposure relative to manual spreadsheet assembly. No comparative pilot establishes a material improvement in accuracy, expert time, deployment friction, price, or partner profit over official tools and existing commercial products.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: DORA reporting is active, official frameworks continue to change, and 2025-2026 remediation and training indicate that the workflow is not fully settled. Conversely, the largest first-cycle error wave may be fading, buyers are learning, and incumbents are already present, so regulatory momentum does not create a clear entrant window by itself.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: An advisor or MSP can theoretically provide one-to-many access and reduce the number of direct end-customer relationships, making the route more compatible with the founder than broad direct sales. No partner has committed, portfolio access and lead flow are unknown, advisors may protect billable work or build internally, and each end client may still require vendor security, audit, and procurement review.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and AI skills fit extraction, entity resolution, validation, and controlled exports, and a synthetic-data prototype is affordable and part-time feasible. Production-grade correctness, regulatory interpretation boundaries, isolated deployments, financial-sector assurance, release responsiveness, liability, partner enablement, and incident support are substantially harder and may exceed one part-time founder's capacity.

highest_value_structural_change: Reduce the product to a signed, self-hosted validation-and-lineage engine that plugs into advisors' existing collection and remediation workflows, and sell it only through anchor partners that prepay a minimum multi-client reporting-cycle commitment. This removes most contract hosting and workflow replacement, makes partner economics observable, and prevents the business from depending on optional per-entity adoption without committed portfolio volume.
main_structural_strength: The partner-aligned, customer-controlled architecture preserves the advisor's service revenue while concentrating the vendor on repeatable provenance, validation, and export infrastructure that can potentially serve multiple regulated entities through each partner.
primary_score_limiter: The critical commercial control point is hypothetical: no advisor has agreed to pay, bring repeat client volume, secure end-client permission, or operate the runtime, and partner intermediation may not remove the underlying vendor's security and procurement burden.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Regulators already provide free templates, data models, validation materials, forms, and training, while ServiceNow and a publicly priced DORA specialist already cover register workflows; this shows that reporting friction can be addressed without the proposed entrant and places direct pressure on both differentiation and price.
